docs.title: Toolbars
docs.text:
• Project: new, open, save, save as, project manager.
  • Format: A2L, OLS, KP, XDF and CSV import buttons.
  • Right-click a toolbar and choose Customize Toolbar… to pick which actions are visible; the choice is persistent (survives restarts).

docs.title: Keyboard
docs.text:
Shortcut Action Ctrl+K Command palette — every command and address is searchable Ctrl+S Save project Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y Undo / redo Ctrl+F Find Ctrl+Tab Cycle open project tabs M / O / D / P Mod / Ori / Δ / % modes in the map editor M / W Widen / narrow the columns in Text and 2D Ctrl+← / Ctrl+→ Shift the origin one byte left / right in Text and 2D F / Shift+F Go to the next / previous map P Toggle the floating 3D Preview window (in the project window) T Switch to the Text view K Turn the selection into a map (Selection → Map) Ctrl+B Optimize value range Ctrl+1 / Ctrl+2 / Ctrl+3 Switch to the Text / 2D / 3D view Ctrl+Shift+F Find bytes… F7 / Shift+F7 Next / previous difference F6 / Shift+F6 Next / previous marker F4 Repeat the last operation (Again) I / S Fill the selection by interpolation / smooth % * / = + - Apply maths to selected cells (a value is asked for)

QAction shortcuts are edited in Miscellaneous ▸ Settings ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts…: a conflict warning appears when a key is already taken, Reset to defaults restores factory values; preferences are persistent.

See the Appendix — menus and shortcuts for the complete list.

docs.title: Rearranging panels
docs.text: Drag panels to move them, float them into their own window or close them. Save the arrangement with Window ▸ Save Workspace Layout.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text: The project file (.mtrp) keeps ROM data, map definitions, edit history and metadata in a single file. You never have to carry the ROM around separately while working.

docs.title: Creating a project
docs.text:
1. Go to Project ▸ New Project.
  2. Pick the ROM file (.bin, .rom, .ori, .mpc, .hex, .s19 …).
  3. The application tries to fill in the ECU type and software number; Brand, Model, Engine and ECU Type are yours to complete.
  4. Save with Project ▸ Save or Ctrl+S.

Where is it stored?

Save the project wherever you like. The application keeps a recent-projects list in the settings; the file itself is portable.

docs.title: OBD unlock (MG1 / MEVD17.2.G)
docs.text:
Project ▸ OBD Unlock (MG1) applies a fixed byte-substitution patch at known offsets for four ECU variants: Gen1 MG1, Gen2 MG1 (pre-2020), Gen2 MG1 (post-2020) and MEVD17.2.G. The ROM is matched by its byte signature first; an unrelated image is refused, and a ROM that is already unlocked is reported as such instead of being patched twice. MEVD17.2.G aborts when more than three patch sites contain unexpected bytes, so a version mismatch can never write blind.

The patch modifies ROM data in memory; nothing is written to disk until you save or export. Check the legal situation in your country before using it — disabling OBD emissions monitoring is restricted in many jurisdictions and will fail an emissions inspection.

docs.title: Version snapshots
docs.text:
Project ▸ Version Snapshot stores the complete state at that moment under a name you choose. Snapshots are:

  • return points (you go back to a chosen version, not to the original),
  • comparable with each other,
  • created automatically by the AI assistant before it applies a change.

Compare two versions with Window ▸ Compare Versions, and two raw ROM files with Project ▸ Compare ROMs.

docs.title: Linked ROMs
docs.text:
If you work with several software versions of the same ECU family, add a reference image with Project ▸ Link ROM to Project:

  • maps in the linked ROM are matched automatically,
  • matching maps open side by side,
  • cursor synchronisation is enabled, so both versions line up row by row.

docs.title: Auto save
docs.text: Miscellaneous ▸ Auto Save writes your edits after a configurable idle time. Auto save writes to temporary files, so a crash does not cost you work.

docs.title: Comparing projects
docs.text:
• Two projects: Window ▸ Compare Projects opens two project windows side by side.
  • Two versions: Window ▸ Compare Versions compares two snapshots of the same project.
  • Differences panel: lists the differences of the selected map.

Comparisons enable synchronised cursors by default; switch them off with Selection ▸ Synchronise Cursors.

docs.title: Project info
docs.text: Miscellaneous ▸ Project Info shows brand, model, engine, ECU type, hardware and software numbers, engine code and notes. These fields are filled from A2L and OLS imports and are exposed as project properties.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
Purpose Output Shareable project .mtrp (default) Raw ROM .bin, .rom WinOLS project .ols TunerPro definition .xdf Map list .csv, .json Tuning report .html

Pick the format from Project ▸ Export. Raw ROM export preserves the original size and byte order; it is only needed when you changed maps.

docs.title: Import
docs.text: MRC Tuner Studio reads many source formats. A2L usually gives the most trustworthy result, because a definition file pins down map addresses, sizes and physical scaling.

docs.title: A2L / DAMOS
docs.text:
The most reliable path. ASAM MCD-2 MC (A2L) is the standard description that ships with the ECU software.

  1. Import the ROM first and create a project.
  2. Choose Project ▸ Import A2L and select the .a2l, .dam or .damos file.
  3. The application resolves the addresses in the A2L against your ROM.

What is taken from the A2L:

A2L construct Use RECORD_LAYOUT Byte size, byte order, signed/unsigned STD_AXIS, COM_AXIS, FIX_AXIS Axis definition and axis scaling COMPU_METHOD Factor that converts to physical values ECU_ADDRESS Base address hint

Base address detection

A2L addresses are relative to a 24-bit or 32-bit base. The application tries a table of common ECU base addresses (MED17, EDC17, ME7, Simos, RH850, MPC …) and picks the one consistent with the ROM size. If needed, correct it manually via View ▸ Data Width and Byte Order.

docs.title: Intel HEX and Motorola S-record
docs.text:
.hex, .s19, .s28 and .s37 files open directly. The application resolves record addresses, preserves gaps and converts the data into a byte array.

HEX output

Writing Intel HEX and S-record is available through the Lua API (writeIntelHex, writeSRecord). Project ▸ Export ROM offers only .bin and .rom.

docs.title: Raw dumps
docs.text:
.bin, .rom, .ori and .mpc files are taken byte for byte. In a raw dump there is no record of where a map starts or ends. In that case:

  1. run Miscellaneous ▸ Auto-detect Maps, or
  2. import an A2L, or
  3. define maps by hand with Find ▸ Map when you know the address.

Auto-detection is a guess: review every map it finds.

docs.title: WinOLS (.ols)
docs.text:
An .ols file is a complete container that includes the ROM data. Import brings across:

  • ROM data,
  • map name, description, address, dimensions, cell size and scaling,
  • axis definitions with their real breakpoint values,
  • vehicle/engine/ECU metadata.

OLS projects containing several firmware versions are imported as a single project with all versions.

Project ▸ Export OLS writes your project back to .ols.

docs.title: KP map packs (.kp)
docs.text:
KP packs carry map definitions, not ROM data, so a project with ROM data must be open before importing. The application

  • resolves addresses against your ROM (scoring Tricore-style 0x80xxxxxx and flat file offsets),
  • drops entries that duplicate maps already in the project,
  • files new maps into folders grouped by name prefix.

Legacy 4.x packs do not always store dimensions; the application recovers columns × rows by matching the product against the cell count.

docs.title: TunerPro (.xdf)
docs.text: .xdf definition files can be imported and exported. On import the mmedtypeflags attribute is decoded, so signed, little-endian and floating point tables are read the way the definition declares them. The BASEOFFSET direction follows its subtract attribute (split 512K/64K definitions use the additive form).

docs.title: OLS map pack (.json)
docs.text: .json map packs produced by WinOLS's "OLS-Files" exporter are read with Project ▸ Import ▸ OLS map pack (JSON). A pack carries map definitions only (address, size, axes, scaling, folder) and no ROM bytes, so it is layered on top of an open ROM. The same definitions can be written back with Project ▸ Export ▸ OLS map pack (JSON) to move the map structure to another WinOLS installation.

docs.title: VAG containers (.frf, .sgo, .odx)
docs.text: .frf, .sgo, .odx and .zip files containing them are supported. Encrypted content requires an external 32-byte AES key/IV file.

docs.title: CSV and JSON map lists
docs.text: Project ▸ Import CSV Map List defines map addresses in bulk from a list file; Export writes the list back out.

docs.title: After importing
docs.text:
• enable Miscellaneous ▸ Auto-scan to run map discovery after each import;
  • if the scaling looks wrong, fix factor and offset in the Map Properties dialog — the displayed values follow it directly.

docs.title: Map editing
docs.text:
An opened map has four views, selected from the tabs at the bottom of its editor: Text (cell table), 2D (curve), 3D (surface) and 3D Sim. All are bound to the same data, so a change in one appears instantly in the others. The full ROM is shown separately as a waveform in the project window's 2d tab (see Interface).

Every view has comparison modes: Mod (current values), Ori (original), Δ (absolute difference) and % (percentage difference). They show you what a tune changed through colour and curves, without reading raw numbers.

docs.title: Text (hex) view
docs.text:
• Offset column on the left, then the bytes, then ASCII or a bar rendering.
  • View ▸ Data Width switches between 8/16/32-bit cells, Byte Order between big and little endian, and Sign between signed and unsigned interpretation.
  • Values can be typed directly into a cell; Enter confirms, Esc cancels.
  • Auto-detected candidate maps are drawn with a thin class-coloured frame + label (amber = Possible, violet = Recognized) and a small Possible/Recognized legend sits at the top-right. Right-clicking a frame promotes the candidate with Add map to list; Show auto maps toggles the whole candidate layer on and off.

docs.title: 2d waveform view (whole ROM)
docs.text:
The byte waveform of the entire ROM, with map blocks drawn as coloured rectangles on top. Use it to move through many maps quickly and to see trends. View ▸ Height Colours changes the colour band.

  • The 8/16/32/F bit and byte-order buttons on the top toolbar drive this view directly (it has no separate selector of its own).
  • A single click only places the cursor — it never changes the view.
  • Double-clicking a map region opens that map's editor and selects the map in the list on the left.
  • Selecting a range with the mouse also selects the same bytes in the Text (hex) view; make a selection in hex and the same range is highlighted in 2D.
  • Switching to the Text tab scrolls the hex view to the same position.
  • The Column guides button on the 2D symbol bar shows/hides the shared Text-view column guides (line breaks) in 2D; the choice is kept between sessions.

docs.title: Column layout and line-break guides
docs.text:
The Text and 2D views share one column layout: change the column count or origin in one and it applies to the other immediately.

  • M widens the columns, W narrows them (WinOLS "more/less columns").
  • Ctrl+← / Ctrl+→ shift the origin one byte left/right, aligning the grid with the start of a map.
  • In the 2D view every column boundary is marked with a vertical line-break guide; every 4th boundary is a bolder major guide. Dragging a guide with the mouse changes the column count directly.
  • Range selections in 2D snap to the line breaks: a selection always starts and ends on a column boundary.
  • When columns are narrower than 3 pixels the guides are hidden for legibility.

docs.title: Map editor tabs
docs.text:
Opening a map (from the map list or by double-clicking in 2D) shows four tabs at the bottom:

Tab Content Text Cell table — the actual editing surface 2D The map's curve, overlaid with the original according to the mode 3D Surface graph; a difference heat map in Δ/Ori mode 3D Sim Sliced/sectioned 3D simulation

On the 2D tab the original ROM is a dashed grey line and the modified ROM a bright line on the same axis; the area between them is shaded red for increases and blue for decreases. In Δ / % mode the curve shows the difference directly, around a zero line. The X axis is labelled with the real axis values (rpm, %, …) when the A2L/OLS data provides them, otherwise with column indices.

  • The Slices checkbox draws each row on its own band (WinOLS 5 "Slices"): in multi-row maps the shapes are compared without overlapping. The choice is persistent — it survives restarts.
  • The Style selector sets the 2D drawing style: Classic (default, plain curve), Columns (per-column separators) or WinOLS (fine value grid + square point markers). The choice is persistent.
  • A statistics row appears on the toolbar for the selected cells: Sel: N · min · max · avg (plus Δavg versus the original, when present). The adjacent heat legend shows the active palette and the current value range.
  • Tune (drag curve): in Mod mode, dragging vertically on the 2D curve writes the selected row's cells directly (drag-to-tune). Writes go through the safe cell-write path with scaling/validation and produce one undo step per drag. Writing is disabled in read-only views (Ori, Δ, %).
  • Hovering shows a crosshair + value readout; the row values for that column (and the original values, if any) are visible.
  • Selecting a column range with the mouse also selects the cells on the Text tab, and vice versa — the 2D and table selections are synchronised.
  • The selected column is highlighted on the 3D surface and in the 3D Sim view.

The 8/16/32/F and byte-order buttons on the top toolbar govern only the whole-ROM Text and 2D views; a map takes its cell type from the map properties.

Closing a project's last map editor clears that project's active-map highlight from the Text, 2D and 3D views.

docs.title: 3d surface view
docs.text:
Shows two-dimensional maps as a surface so you can judge gradients by colour and height. Editing happens on the Text tab.

When you switch to Δ or Ori mode, the surface colours the signed difference between the original and the modified data: increases red, decreases blue, with the colour intensity scaled by the magnitude of the difference. That answers "where and how much changed" in 3D at a glance. Mod mode returns you to the normal height heat map. The tinting works in both the 3D and 3D-sim views, which also gained soft directional lighting and specular shading.

docs.title: Floating 3D Preview
docs.text: View ▸ 3D Preview opens a free-floating 3D preview window for the selected map; it follows the current map as you browse the map list. Four render themes are available under View ▸ 3D Preview Theme: Dark, Blue Mesh, Green and White. The choice is persistent.

docs.title: Comparison modes (Mod / Ori / Δ / %)
docs.text:
The map editor toolbar has four mode buttons:

Button Shortcut Shows Mod M Modified/current values (editable) Ori O Original ROM values (read-only) Δ D Cell-by-cell absolute difference: Mod − Ori % P Cell-by-cell percentage difference
  • Increases versus the original are tinted warm (red/orange) and decreases cold (blue); changed cells get a triangular delta flag in the corner.
  • Ori, Δ and % modes are read-only — no accidental writes; return to Mod mode to edit.
  • In Δ / % mode a delta summary row appears on the top toolbar: changed / total cells, percentage, min/avg/max difference.
  • The Physical / Raw Hex / Raw Dec selector chooses whether values are shown in physical units or as raw storage bits.

docs.title: Editing tools
docs.text:
Operations from the Edit menu apply to the selection or to the whole map:

Operation Effect Value +1 / −1 Increment or decrement selected cells Absolute change Write a single value Relative change Add a percentage or an absolute delta Slider limits Lock cells to a range Round Round values to a step Restore original Return selected cells to their original values Interpolation Generate a linear or exponential ramp between two points Smooth Smooth neighbouring values Flatten Flatten the values Repeat last operation Apply the same edit again

Every edit can be undone: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y.

Common operations also have shortcuts: + / - value +1/−1, = absolute value, % relative change, F4 repeat the last operation (Again) and F11 restore the original value. Edit ▸ Insert New Hexdump opens an extra hex window.

Edit ▸ Edit history… lists every transaction (with its description and byte range). Double-clicking a step rolls the ROM straight to that point — the hex, 2D and 3D views refresh instantly.

docs.title: Quick keyboard editing
docs.text:
With cells selected in the map table you apply maths directly by pressing a key; a small dialog asks for the value:

Key Action % or * Scale selected cells by a percentage (105 → +5%) / Apply a division ratio = Set all selected cells to an absolute value + / - Increment / decrement in fine steps I Interpolate between the selection ends (fill in intermediate values) S 3×3 weighted smoothing filter Enter / F2 Open the inline cell editor; Enter confirms and moves down a row Esc Cancel the edit Arrow keys Move between cells; Shift extends the selection

docs.title: Selection menu
docs.text:
The Selection menu works in both the Text and 2D views:

Command Effect Select Cell / Column / Row / Screen / Nothing Select a cell / column / row / screen, or clear the selection Invert Selection Invert the current selection Restore Last Selection Bring back the previous selection Selection to Start / End Move the selection to the start / end of the ROM Save / Load Selection… Save / load the selection to a .sel file Selection → Map… (K) Turn the selected byte range into a new map Support map selection Estimate the column count + origin for the selected range

Support map selection tries to fit the byte block you selected onto a WinOLS-style grid: it finds the most likely column count and origin and applies them.

docs.title: Region edits
docs.text: Select a cell range to change only part of a map. Patch and pack files describe the same with row_start, row_end, col_start and col_end, so only that region is written instead of the whole map.

docs.title: Working with scaling
docs.text:
You see values in the physical domain (bar, °C …); the application converts them to raw bytes through the scaling rule. Change scaling in the Map Properties dialog instead of scaling by hand:

  • Factor and offset,
  • Byte order — in some A2L files the cell bytes are reversed,
  • the unit label.

If the scaling is wrong, every edit is written wrong — which is why importing from A2L is the preferred path.

docs.title: Map properties
docs.text: Double-click a map to open its properties: name, description, unit, start address, type (MAP / CURVE / VALUE), dimensions and scaling. The From hexdump cursor button next to the address field assigns the address you are currently on in the hex view.

docs.title: Find and replace
docs.text:
The Find menu covers:

  • Address — a given offset,
  • Value — cells containing a number,
  • Map — search and filter by name,
  • Similar files — find similar ROMs,
  • Find bytes… (Ctrl+Shift+F) — search the active ROM for a hex byte sequence, with ?? wildcard bytes. Matches are listed in a results dialog; clicking one jumps the hex view to that address.
  • Replace bytes… — replace every match with a new sequence; all changes form a single undo step.
  • Next comment / Previous comment — step through the comments in the project.
  • Comments and markers — annotate and navigate.

docs.title: Differences to original, printing and axis profiles
docs.text:
• View ▸ Differences to Original… opens a dialog listing the changed cells; click a row to jump to that address.
  • View ▸ Next Difference / Previous Difference (F7 / Shift+F7) step through the differences.
  • Project ▸ Print… sends the tuning report to a printer or PDF.
  • Project ▸ Export tune report as PDF… writes the same tuning report directly to a .pdf file.
  • Project ▸ Export A2L (DAMOS)… exports the project's maps as an ASAP2/DAMOS .a2l description file (the counterpart to Import A2L).
  • View ▸ Compare two maps… opens a dialog that compares two maps side by side, cell by cell, with difference colours.
  • Project ▸ Save axis profile… / Load axis profile… saves and restores the active map's X/Y axis descriptors (name, unit, values).

docs.title: Excel and CSV export
docs.text:
Two spreadsheet exports live in the Project menu:

  • Export map list as Excel… — writes the map list (name, address, size, scaling …) as a single .xls file.
  • Export map values… — asks for a folder and writes the cell values of every map in the project as one CSV file per map into that folder, for inspection in a spreadsheet or processing with external tools.

docs.title: Sample tuning packs
docs.text:
data/tuningpacks/ holds sample .mtrpack templates derived from EDC16/EDC17 tuning guides. They carry map definitions only (addresses are 0x000000 placeholders, scales/sizes are estimates) and contain no ROM bytes.

⚠️ The addresses, sizes and scalings are unverified. Do not use any map without validating it against your own ECU/software version and A2L/DAMOS file; a wrong application can brick an ECU.

Import: Project ▸ Import Map Pack… → pick the file → tick the maps to include. Because it is definition-only, the button reads Add selected to project; only the definitions are added and no ROM byte is written.

docs.title: ECU presets
docs.text:
Project ▸ Apply ECU preset… lists the JSON presets under data/ecupresets/ (the application reads them from disk, so adding a preset needs no rebuild).

  • Selecting a preset shows its checksum hint; the settings fields are written to empty project fields only (e.g. ecuType, ecuProducer).
  • If mapPack is set, the normal Import Map Pack dialog opens; you still pick which maps to apply.
  • Presets with verified: false appear with an (unverified) tag and raise a warning in the dialog.

⚠️ These presets are unverified skeletons: they contain no real ROM data, verified address, size or scaling. Validate every value against your own ECU/software version and A2L/DAMOS file.

docs.title: Auto-map (database) — catalogue-driven map inference
docs.text:
Miscellaneous ▸ Auto-map (database)… combines a map-definition catalogue (data/ecukb/mapdefs.db, produced by tools/dataset/build_mapdefs.py) with the ROM's blind structural scanner.

  • Family-aware inference: the catalogue returns the maps that belong to the matching HW/SW number and ECU family. When the project family is empty it is resolved from the software number.
  • Offset/sector-shift alignment: when the target ROM comes from a different read method or software revision, every row's address is re-validated with a fingerprint + value signature and shifted to its real location (Relocation).
  • Blend with blind detection: regions the catalogue cannot cover are filled in by blind auto-detection; overlapping hits raise confidence.
  • Review → add to project: results appear in a sortable table with name, type, address, size, confidence and source (Database / Auto-detect / both); every row is selected up front. Deselect what you do not want and click Add selected to project. Added maps land in the Auto-inferred folder.
  • The ROM is unchanged: adding maps only grows the project's map list; no ROM byte is written and no undo step is created.

When the catalogue is absent (mapdefs.db not found) the tool shows blind auto-detection results only. Generate the catalogue data locally with tools/dataset/build_mapdefs.py as described in DATASET_SETUP.md.

docs.title: Maintenance mode (data-driven maintenance operations)
docs.text:
Project ▸ Maintenance mode… lists maintenance operations such as DPF / EGR / AdBlue / Lambda / TVA / Flaps from the catalogue under data/tuningops/*.json. The catalogue is read from disk, so adding a JSON file needs no rebuild. The list is first filtered by the active project's ECU family; the Show all ECU families checkbox reveals the whole catalogue.

  • Each operation is listed with its brand, family, patch count, confidence value and — where applicable — an [UNVERIFIED] tag. The row tooltip carries the source file, software reference and read method.
  • Checking one or more operations activates the Preview pane: the Relocation (offset/sector-shift) report — matched, shifted, ambiguous and not found counts plus a confidence percentage — and the affected maps. Relocation first tries the patch's recorded offset; failing that it searches a bounded window around it for the byte/anchor pattern, so a patch can be carried across a software version where the address moved.
  • Apply writes the resolved patches of the selected operations to the ROM as a single undo step. If an unverified operation is selected the confirmation dialog calls it out.
  • After applying, the application checks the checksum automatically: it reports when the checksum is still valid, suggests Project ▸ Correct Checksum… when it is invalid, and raises a could not be verified warning when there is no family definition (see Verification).

⚠️ The operation catalogue may be unverified (verified: false). Do not apply any operation without validating it against your own ECU/software version and A2L/DAMOS file.

docs.title: Change Recorder panel
docs.text:
View ▸ Change Recorder (hidden by default) opens a panel that records ROM edits live:

  • Start recording / Stop recording toggles capture; the status line shows how many changes were captured.
  • The list shows each edit with its offset, length and before → after bytes; the full byte string is in the row tooltip.
  • Copy puts the recording on the clipboard as a Lua script; Create script… writes the same content to a file as Lua or .mtrpatch text (the same as Create script from changes… in the Project menu).
  • Clear empties the recording.

docs.title: A safe editing routine
docs.text:
1. Take a Project ▸ Version Snapshot before you start.
  2. Begin with a small region and verify the result with measurements.
  3. When you are done, package it as a .mtrpatch — the question "which ROM did I apply this to?" answers itself later.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: After you change a ROM the ECU will still load it, but it may fail safety or emissions tests. Verification does two things: it proves your data landed in the right place, and it recalculates the checksum areas.

docs.title: What is a checksum?
docs.text: Many ECUs carry an integrity value over their code and data blocks, either inside the block or at its end. If that value does not change, the ECU assumes nothing was modified. Writing invalidates it; if you do not correct it, the ECU makes that decision for you (usually by entering a limp mode).

docs.title: Verify and correct
docs.text:
Project ▸ Verify Checksum checks every block for the selected algorithm. Project ▸ Correct Checksum recomputes the blocks that fail.

Workflow:

  1. Select your ECU type.
  2. Run Verify; the failing blocks are listed.
  3. Make your map edits first and run the checksum correction last — otherwise the checksum becomes invalid again.
  4. Verify once more after correcting.

docs.title: The checksum dialog
docs.text:
Project ▸ Verify/Correct Checksum opens a WinOLS-style table window:

Column Meaning # Row number Algorithm Algorithm name From / To Covered address range Manually Manually added entry AutoCorr. Automatic correction enabled

Buttons: Search (re-detect on this ROM), Add… (manually add an algorithm from the installed list), Properties… (details of the selected entry), Delete (remove a manually added entry), Apply (recalculate checksums in memory) and Installed plugins… (installed checksum modules). Apply produces a single undo step, and — as the note at the bottom of the dialog says — checksums are recalculated automatically at export.

docs.title: The Checksums panel and status bar
docs.text:
Project ▸ Checksums (or View ▸ Checksums) opens a persistent dock on the right (hidden by default). The panel auto-detects the active ROM and shows one row per checksum engine (native Specs first, then DLL algorithms):

Column Meaning # Row number Algorithm / Engine Algorithm or engine name Family Matched ECU family From / To Covered address range Status ok / mismatch / unknown Correctable Whether this row may be corrected safely
  • Verify only computes; it never touches the ROM.
  • Correct & Apply rewrites only the correctable rows and commits them all as a single undo step.
  • Refresh re-runs detection; the panel refreshes itself (debounced) when the project changes or the ROM is edited.

A WinOLS-style live readout sits at the right of the status bar and updates after edits:

  • All CS ok — Checksum block N: okay — every block is valid,
  • CS mismatch — N issue(s) — a mismatch exists,
  • No checksum module — no engine for this family,
  • CS: unknown (no definition) — an engine exists but the family has no definition.

docs.title: Automatic correction at export
docs.text:
With Project ▸ Correct checksums on export (checkable) enabled, every detected checksum block is corrected automatically when a ROM is exported — on the exported copy only; the project ROM is never modified. When it is off, the application asks whether to correct before writing.

Every ROM export is preceded by a preview dialog showing the file name, the size and the current checksum state — valid, invalid — will be corrected on export, invalid — you will be prompted to correct it or cannot be verified. If no algorithm is detected the correction is skipped and a status-bar warning is shown; the export is not blocked.

docs.title: Family definitions and the "could not be verified" state
docs.text:
The final pre-export check also consults the optional ECU family checksum catalogue (data/ecukb/checksum_families.json), which maps an ECU family to a human-readable algorithm hint. The application distinguishes two cases:

  • Algorithm known but not detected — the catalogue has a hint for the family; the export proceeds and Correct Checksum… is suggested.
  • No family definition — there is no catalogue match; the checksum is flagged as could not be verified and the ROM is exported unchanged. You must verify the checksum yourself before flashing.

When the catalogue is absent this distinction cannot be made and the feature silently disappears; the export is still not blocked.

docs.title: Bosch MED17 / EDC17 checksums and the CVN signature
docs.text:
MED17/EDC17 images do not carry a single checksum: the flash is split into blocks, each with its own CRC32 (polynomial 0x04C11DB7, MSB first), plus a customer block and a 1024-bit RSA signature (the CVN the tester reads over OBD). The built-in engine parses the TriCore block descriptors, verifies and rewrites the block CRCs, and re-derives the customer block. On an unrecognised image it reports InvalidFormat and never writes a byte — a blind checksum pass over a real ECU image would brick it.

Because the RSA block is recalculated after the block CRCs are corrected, the CVN stays consistent with the modified flash instead of exposing the file as "modified" to a diagnostic tester.

docs.title: Built-in (native) checksum engine
docs.text:
The application ships a config-driven native checksum engine that needs no DLL. The family-to-algorithm mapping is read from data/ecukb/native_checksums.json (produced by tools/dataset/build_native_checksums.py). The engine supports additive (Sum8/16/32), XOR and CRC kinds (CCITT/IBM/IEEE plus custom parameters).

  • Native first, DLL as fallback: when a family has a native definition the native engine is tried first; with no definition the Windows module library is used.
  • Safe correction: the native engine writes only for Specs marked correctable whose blocks fall inside the ROM; for an unknown family verification returns known=false and no byte is changed.

Bosch MED17/EDC17 verification and correction are also embedded; no DLL is required. Every other family uses the Windows module library.

docs.title: Checksum coverage
docs.text: Family-to-algorithm knowledge has been enriched through WinOLS checksum modules, Ecus.txt/Modelle.txt, FTAG and web research. Current coverage: 152 families (checksum_families.json), 113 WinOLS families (winols_checksum_families.json) and 13 native algorithms (native_checksums.json). The coverage data is optional; without it the readout says "no definition" (see DATASET_SETUP.md for setup).

docs.title: The 148-module Windows library
docs.text:
ChecksumDLL/ contains 148 32-bit modules. They run on 32-bit Windows and are invoked from the 64-bit application through the checksumhelper.exe helper process.

Required runtime

The modules depend on the Microsoft Visual C++ 2005 SP1 (x86) runtime. Without it they fail to load, and the application reports that explicitly.

The modules only work on Windows; on Linux and macOS only the built-in MED17/EDC17 path is available.

docs.title: Why a separate process for loading a module?
docs.text: checksumhelper.exe is a 32-bit helper. ROM data travels between the two processes through temporary files, which lets a 64-bit application run a 32-bit DLL without loading it into its own address space.

docs.title: Version Overview (version comparison matrix)
docs.text: View ▸ Version Overview… opens a matrix whose rows are maps and whose columns are versions: each cell shows how many bytes of that map changed in that version relative to the original. The version selector + note row at the top edits the comment (note) of each version. Project ▸ Save Version Snapshot… generates the note automatically — summarising how many maps and bytes changed in the form "N map(s), M byte(s) changed"; you can edit it freely afterwards.

docs.title: Accept changes (transfer operations from another project)
docs.text: Project ▸ Accept Changes from Project… transfers edits from another .mtrp project into the current one. Matching is done by value pattern, not by address, so operations are applied location-independently even when the source project's maps sit at different addresses.

docs.title: Watermark (digital signature)
docs.text: Project ▸ Sign ROM (Watermark)… embeds an invisible ownership signature into the ROM's largest empty (0x00/0xFF) region; it changes neither normal reading nor driving behaviour. Project ▸ Verify Watermark finds and verifies the signature, so you can later prove that a file came from your bench.

docs.title: Processor detection
docs.text: Miscellaneous ▸ Detect processor… scans the ROM for known signatures and reports a CPU-family estimate with a confidence percentage. It is a quick pre-check to confirm the ECU family before picking a checksum algorithm.

docs.title: Always cross-check externally
docs.text:
Treat the application's result as one opinion among several:

  • the ECU vendor's own tool set,
  • the manufacturer's checksum/validation software,
  • dyno and emissions test results.

Even if the application reports success, wrong address matching makes the whole chain meaningless. The weakest link in verification is not the checksum — it is address matching.

docs.title: A2L base address verification
docs.text:
Addresses in an A2L file are relative to a base address. With the wrong base, maps open in the wrong place and checksum verification will not notice. On the first run:

  1. Compare an address you know with the A2L value.
  2. Confirm the ROM holds meaningful data at that address.
  3. Correct the base address list manually if necessary.

docs.title: Save and reopen test
docs.text:
The simplest integrity test:

  1. Save your changes.
  2. Close the project.
  3. Open the file again.
  4. Run Verify and check the values in the maps you edited.

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text: Making a change in one ROM is easy. Making the same change in ten ROMs is not. Packaging collects your edits into one file that can be applied to other ROM versions.

docs.title: Two formats, two purposes
docs.text: Format Contains Use when .mtrpack Map names, addresses, scaling and new values Carrying work to other ROM versions .mtrpatch Map cell patches and optional raw byte patches Repeating the exact same edit

docs.title: Map packs (.mtrpack)
docs.text:
Export

  1. Go to Project ▸ Export Map Pack.
  2. Select the maps to include.
  3. Save as .mtrpack or as CSV.

Import and apply

  1. Project ▸ Import Map Pack and pick the file.
  2. Review the maps in the list.
  3. Press Apply selected to ROM.

Matching happens in three steps: explicit address, name, then the address stored in the pack. Dimension mismatches and byte-order differences are reported as warnings; you can still apply.

docs.title: ROM patches (.mtrpatch)
docs.text:
Patches are editable JSON documents. Besides map cell patches they may contain raw byte patches outside map regions.

Careful: raw byte changes (for example ECU-specific checksum/CRC areas) are only correct for the same software version and the same base ROM. Applying them to a different base produces wrong checksums. In that case choose "apply maps only".

Applying

  1. Open the patch with Project ▸ Patch Editor.
  2. Match maps by name and address; a CRC mismatch is a warning, not an error.
  3. Large patches ask you to type APPLY.
  4. A "Before patch: …" version snapshot is offered.
  5. The Patch Results dialog summarises how many maps applied cleanly, with warnings, and which failed.

docs.title: Map lists (CSV / JSON)
docs.text:
Two different CSV features — do not confuse them:

  • Map list — map names and addresses, also exportable as JSON, useful for lists produced by external tools.
  • CSV data list — plain text export and import of the cells of one map.

docs.title: Tuning report (HTML)
docs.text: Project ▸ Tuning Report writes your changes into a readable HTML document: old and new values, map addresses, notes. Practical for a customer handover or your own records.

docs.title: Other exports
docs.text: Purpose File WinOLS project .ols TunerPro definition .xdf Map list .csv, .json Report .html Theme sharing .mtrtheme

docs.title: Packaging discipline
docs.text:
1. Build a pack for one topic ("Stage 1 — low RPM fuel maps").
  2. Write down why each pack exists.
  3. Test on a flashed ROM first, then on the real vehicle.
  4. Keep packs in version control; one day you will need to know which pack you applied and when.

docs.title: AI assistant
docs.text: The assistant sees your real project data through tools. It does not guess: before it changes anything it states what it is about to do and asks for your approval.

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
Provider Note Claude, OpenAI, Qwen, DeepSeek, Gemini, Groq Require an API key Ollama, LM Studio Run locally, no key needed OpenCode Zen / Go Works with OpenCode credentials Custom endpoint Any OpenAI-compatible URL

Key, base URL and model are set in the settings (Ayarlar ▸ AI). For OpenCode the credentials can be imported straight from the TUI with Import from opencode TUI. Model lists are fetched live from the provider; the ⟳ button refreshes them.

docs.title: OpenCode Bridge — the recommended path for free models
docs.text:
The opencode.ai free tier verifies that a request really comes from the official OpenCode client (Cloudflare TLS/JA3-JA4 fingerprinting, HTTP/2 frame analysis, the User-Agent header and the tool declarations in the body). Spoofing headers therefore does not work.

The OpenCode Bridge does not spoof — it uses the real client. The official opencode binary is started in the background as a local HTTP server (opencode serve) and the application only ever talks to it over 127.0.0.1. The upstream call is made by the official client, so the fingerprint problem disappears.

  • Install: npm install -g opencode-ai (the app finds the binary automatically).
  • No credentials needed: sign-in lives in OpenCode's own auth store (run opencode auth login once).
  • The bridge launches the server with its own private configuration: the user's own MCP servers are disabled and only MRC's ROM tool server is registered. Reason: the free tier rejects requests carrying more than 128 tool definitions, and an installation with several MCP servers registered crosses that limit instantly, failing every -free model.
  • Default endpoint http://127.0.0.1:41999, configurable under Settings → AI.

MCP tools work in bridge mode too

The bridge registers MRC's own MCP server (mtrmcp.exe, 82 ROM tools) in the OpenCode configuration automatically. Free models can call list_maps, get_map_values, set_map_values, compare_map_values, scan_dtcs and the rest directly. Opening a project binds the tool server to that project; if you switch projects, the bridge restarts the server on the next message so the tools follow the new project. If the tool server ever dies (crash, mtrmcp.exe rebuild, antivirus), the bridge reconnects it automatically on the next message; you do not need to restart the application.

Your data boundaries

API keys stay on your machine. When you select a provider, the conversation and the tool results are sent to that provider. Use a local provider (Ollama / LM Studio) for sensitive projects.

docs.title: Permission modes
docs.text: Mode Behaviour Ask Every write tool raises an approval card. Default and recommended. Auto No approval card, but the validation layers still run. Plan Write tools are locked; the model may only propose a plan.

docs.title: Tools (71)
docs.text:
They fall into five groups:

Discovery — map search, listing by name, map properties, axes, folders, statistics.

Reading — current and original values, raw ROM reads, similarity search, anomaly detection, shape analysis.

Writing — fill a whole map, write a cell range, scale, offset, clamp, smooth, apply an expression, copy a map, undo.

Management — version snapshots, linked-ROM operations, comments, dyno results.

Planning — plan_start, plan_propose, plan_list, plan_remove, plan_review, plan_finalize, plan_apply.

docs.title: Selecting a map: by name or by address
docs.text:
The map tools (get_map_info, get_map_values, get_original_values, get_axis_values, get_map_statistics, set_map_values, …) accept two ways of picking a map:

  • map_name — the map name; if it is ambiguous a candidate list comes back.
  • address — an address such as 0x00009174; when the address is unique the result is exact.

When a name is ambiguous the tool returns a candidates array. Every candidate carries address (hex) and addressDec (number), so the next call can use the address directly. The address format is identical across every tool: address is always an 8-digit uppercase hex string, addressDec is always an integer.

docs.title: Byte order and scaling
docs.text:
The byte order can differ per map family within one ROM. The tool layer no longer uses the global project byte order — it uses the map's own order (MapInfo::cellBigEndian). A2L carries no per-map byte order, so the project setting applies there. Axis points follow the same rule.

Read responses are enriched so a result can be verified:

Field Meaning dataSize Cell size in bytes signed Whether the cell is signed effectiveByteOrder The byte order actually used for the read raw Raw cell bytes ("6F 6F") scaling Scaling: coeffA, offset, formula, unit scalingKnown Whether a scaling definition exists valuesAreRaw Without scaling the values are raw storage integers

When scalingKnown is false the values array is not in physical units — it holds raw storage integers, and the response says so in note. A unit mistake such as "degrees instead of °C" therefore cannot pass silently.

docs.title: Plan-first workflow
docs.text:
Put the assistant in Plan mode for large changes. The model follows:

  1. plan_start — opens a session, creates mrc_plan.json and plan.md.
  2. plan_propose — adds a justified proposal per change.
  3. plan_review — lists the proposals so you can drop what you do not want.
  4. plan_finalize — freezes the plan; write tools stay locked.
  5. plan_apply — runs only with confirm=true and only after your approval.

The application takes a snapshot before applying and writes no byte until these checks pass:

  • scaling and byte-order validation,
  • physical value bounds, rejection of NaN/infinite values,
  • rejection of scale factors outside 0.5–3.0,
  • map dimensions versus target ROM size.

docs.title: Example requests
docs.text:
Find the catalyst monitoring maps in this ROM and zero their thresholds.
Increase the fuel pump map flow by 8%, plan first.
Smooth the high-RPM region of the injection maps.

The first writes (with approval), the second works in plan mode, the third is limited to a single map. The narrower you write the request, the more reviewable the result.

docs.title: Map name translation
docs.text:
Miscellaneous ▸ Translate Map Names translates map names and descriptions into your target language. The engine chain is Google → Google (Chrome) → MyMemory, and results are cached in the mapnames database.

The live preview table shows Original | Translated columns and the translation column is editable. Remove results you do not like with Miscellaneous ▸ Clear Translation Cache.

docs.title: Chat history
docs.text: Chats are stored per project and restored when you reopen it. The history panel lets you return to earlier sessions.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The assistant only reaches the open project's data; it does not roam the file system.
  • Write tools cannot bypass the validation layers.
  • Every change the AI makes can be reverted with Ctrl+Z — each write leaves a reversible ROM record behind. The Modified filter and the "Mod (N)" counter in the left panel update right away; you do not have to restart the program.
  • It cannot guarantee that a safety or emissions test will pass — do not decide without measuring.

docs.title: MCP server (external AI agents)
docs.text:
MRC Tuner Studio includes a headless Model Context Protocol (MCP) server binary named mtrmcp.exe. External AI agents such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, OpenCode, and Cursor can connect directly to the ROM engine through this server.

  • Menu access: AI ▸ MCP Server & AI Integrations (Claude, OpenCode)…
  • Dialog controls: Start and stop the headless server with one click, inspect live stdout/stderr logs, configure Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and OpenCode automatically, or copy generic JSON snippets.
  • 82 tools: Exposes a full suite of tools including map listing/reading/writing, ROM byte search/replacement, DTC scanning (scan_dtcs) and enabling/disabling (set_dtc_status), checksum verification (verify_checksums), automatic map discovery (scan_rom_maps), version snapshots, and the plan-first workflow.
  • Structured responses: Every response also carries the payload as a real JSON object in structuredContent, so a client no longer has to parse the text JSON a second time.
  • Write policy: --bypass-dialogs (the default) applies write tools directly and never opens a modal dialog. --confirm refuses to write and returns {"status":"confirmation_required"} with the ROM provably untouched. --read-only does not advertise write tools at all.
  • Read-only guarantee: The guarantee now also covers the edge cases — logbook writes (append_tuning_note, log_dyno_result), checksum correction (verify_checksums with correct), ROM scanning, target-ROM selection and closing the project.
  • Undo / redo / status: undo_last_change, redo and project_status manage the project state and history; project_status also reports how many maps were modified.
  • Structured folders: list_folders and get_folder_maps return key, description and parent separately for every folder, so a composite KEY: "description" name no longer has to be parsed by hand. Exposes a full suite of tools including map listing/reading/writing, ROM byte search/replacement, DTC scanning (scan_dtcs) and enabling/disabling (set_dtc_status), checksum verification (verify_checksums), automatic map discovery (scan_rom_maps), version snapshots, and the plan-first workflow.
  • Security: "Read-only mode" in the dialog is ENABLED by default; mutating tools are excluded from discovery and rejected if called. In write mode, an automatic reversible version snapshot is taken prior to every write.
  • CLI usage: Can be run standalone via mtrmcp.exe --project <file.mtrp> or in read-only mode via mtrmcp.exe --read-only.

docs.title: Automation
docs.text: Instead of doing repetitive work by hand you can script it: batch edits, exports, comparisons and even simple HTTP requests.

docs.title: Command palette
docs.text:
Ctrl+K — every command in the application appears in one searchable list. Typing part of a command name is enough. It is the fastest way to find an action without knowing the menus.

The palette also supports direct address jumps: typing 0x1A400, $1A400 or a bare hex value puts an Address: Jump to 0x… entry at the top of the list; Enter jumps the active project's Hex and 2d views to that address.

Map search results draw a small curve sparkline sampled from the ROM data for each map, so you can see its shape without opening it.

docs.title: Lua engine
docs.text: The application embeds Lua 5.4 and binds the C++ API to scripts through sol2. Run a script with Datalog ▸ Run Lua Script.

docs.title: What is available
docs.text:
• read project properties,
  • read and write bytes, convert addresses,
  • search maps, find and replace, import and export,
  • add comments, similarity search,
  • HTTP requests,
  • open dialogs, call the interface.

docs.title: Security limits
docs.text:
Scripts run on a worker thread and return to the UI only through controlled calls. The engine disables:

  • os.execute, os.exit, io.popen, package.loadlib, dofile, loadfile, load
  • os.remove, os.rename and os.tmpname outside approved paths

Running a new script for the first time requires confirmation, and the trust decision is stored with the script's SHA-256 fingerprint.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
-- List every map whose name contains "KRKTE"
local maps = searchMaps("KRKTE")
for _, m in ipairs(maps) do
  Log(m.name .. " @ " .. m.address)
end

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: The Lua checksum DSL, projectImportCsvJson, projectMail, some WinOLS-specific rights and vehicle-data operations and encrypted .luax loading are not implemented.

docs.title: Debug RPC (developer channel)
docs.text: Builds with MTR_DEBUG_RPC=ON open a line-delimited JSON channel on 127.0.0.1:48714. The channel is meant for automation and testing; it is disabled in Release builds.

docs.title: Map-aware writing
docs.text:
The older apply_edit command works on a byte range and uses the display setting's cell size — on a 16-bit map it truncated the value to a single byte and left the high byte at its stale ROM value. The new set_map_values command uses the map's own cell size, byte order and signedness:

{"cmd":"set_map_values","args":{"sub":0,"map":"Boost target","value":3500,"absolute":true}}

The response contains the raw bytes that were written, so the write can be verified:

{"ok":true,"result":{"raw":"F5 24","bytesWritten":"F5 24","dataSize":2,
 "byteOrder":"little-endian","signed":true,"cellCount":1}}

If the value does not fit the cell the command returns an error — there is no silent truncation:

{"ok":false,"error":"value 40000 does not fit in a 2-byte signed cell"}

Pass "clamp":true to clamp instead; the result then reports clamped:true.

docs.title: Repairing a map
docs.text:
Command What it does map_info The full map record: dataSize, signed, byteOrder, effectiveByteOrder, scaling set_map_byte_order Changes one map's byte order; the global setting is untouched set_map_scaling Fixes one map's scaling (coeffA, offset, unit) action {"trigger":"m_actSave"} Saves the project

set_map_byte_order and set_map_scaling are persistent: they are written to the project file. map_info additionally reports the project byte order (projectByteOrder) and the map's own byte order (mapByteOrder) separately; when they differ, the map is read with its own order.

docs.title: Datalog
docs.text:
Datalog ▸ Open Log opens CSV recordings; pick channels from the tree and read the time-series graphs. Datalog ▸ Compare Logs overlays two recordings.

Three source formats are recognised automatically:

  • Vehical — three header rows (name / description / unit), first column Time in milliseconds.
  • Autotuner — single header row starting with timestamp, units embedded in the column names as (unit).
  • VCDS (Ross-Tech) measuring-block logs — every measuring group has its own TIME/STAMP column and samples on its own clock. The groups are merged onto one time axis by linear interpolation, so a VCDS export can be compared against a map directly. European exports write decimal commas; both 0.96 and 0,96 are accepted.

docs.title: A practical order of preference for bulk work
docs.text:
1. Does an external tool already do it?
  2. Is the application's packaging feature enough?
  3. Does the command palette solve it in one step?
  4. Only then write a Lua script.

docs.title: Before you script something
docs.text:
1. Do not repeat a manual job: package it (see Packaging).
  2. Write a script only for genuinely repetitive multi-step work.
  3. Keep scripts in version control and comment which map addresses they touch.

docs.title: MCP server for external AI agents
docs.text: To delegate automation tasks to external AI agents (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, etc.) or automate operations via the command line, use the built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. For details and tool listings, see AI assistant — MCP server.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Miscellaneous ▸ Settings manages language, theme, AI providers, paths and advanced options.

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
The interface language changes instantly from Miscellaneous ▸ Language. Six language packages ship in the repository:

tr · en · es · nl · th · zh_CN

The interface language and map-name translation are different things: the interface comes from the settings, map names from Miscellaneous ▸ Translate Map Names.

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
The default theme is the MRC palette: dark background with green and orange accents. Other palettes are available in the ColorThemes list.

A theme change is applied immediately: window chrome, waveform view, curve colours, chat bubbles/panels (including the guided-workflow cards) and map rows are repainted. Labels such as From hexdump cursor are re-coloured as well.

docs.title: Colours
docs.text:
Every theme colour under Settings ▸ Colours/Theme is editable with a visual colour picker. A new Comparison Delta Colors group selects the increase (warm) / decrease (cool) delta colours. The background colour of the Overview / minimap strip right of the hex view is set in the same dialog.

User themes can be saved, renamed, deleted and exported/imported as .mtrtheme files.

To create a custom palette, edit mrcSignature() in appconfig.cpp and rebuild.

docs.title: Map heat display
docs.text:
The map-editor grid and both 3D surface views share one heat palette, chosen under Settings ▸ Map heat display:

Palette Character MRC Default: navy → teal → green → amber → coral Viridis Perceptually uniform, colour-blind friendly Turbo High-contrast rainbow Grayscale Grey tones for print / e-ink Classic OLS Classic blue → green → yellow → red

The delta threshold sets what fraction of the map's largest change the 3D delta view should ignore (0 % shows everything). While the delta view is active a red/blue difference scale (Δ Mod−Ori) is drawn in the corner.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
The Settings ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts… dialog edits QAction shortcuts: a conflict warning appears when a key is already taken, Reset to defaults restores factory values. Preferences are persistent.

The new grid and navigation keys ship as defaults and can be changed in the same dialog:

Shortcut Action M / W Widen / narrow the columns in Text and 2D Ctrl+← / Ctrl+→ Shift the origin one byte left / right F / Shift+F Next / previous map P / T 3D Preview / Text view K Selection → Map Ctrl+B Optimize value range

docs.title: Column layout (shared Text / 2D grid)
docs.text:
The Text and 2D views share a single column layout: M/W change the column count and Ctrl+←/Ctrl+→ change the origin. In 2D the column boundaries are drawn as line-break guides (every 4th is major), and you can drag a guide to change the column count directly. The layout is kept for the session; Selection ▸ Support map selection finds the most likely column + origin for a selected range.

The 2D curve style is set by the Style selector in the map editor: Classic (default), Columns or WinOLS; Reset to defaults restores Classic. The Column guides button in the workspace 2D view shows/hides the shared column guides; the preference is kept between sessions.

docs.title: Toolbar customisation
docs.text: Right-click a toolbar and choose Customize Toolbar… to pick which actions are visible; preferences are persistent.

docs.title: 3D preview theme
docs.text: View ▸ 3D Preview Theme selects the render theme of the floating 3D Preview window: Dark, Blue Mesh, Green and White. The choice is persistent and independent of the map heat palette (a separate surface colouring).

docs.title: ECU presets and workspace layouts
docs.text:
• ECU presets: Project ▸ Apply ECU preset… reads the JSON presets under data/ecupresets/; the MTR_DATA_DIR environment variable can point at a custom data root. Presets fill empty project fields only, show a checksum hint and flag unverified entries with a warning.
  • Layout presets: Window ▸ Save Layout as… stores the current dock arrangement as a named preset (key ui/layouts/<name>); restore it from the Restore Layout submenu and remove it with Delete Layout….

docs.title: Data root, knowledge base and offline translation
docs.text:
• Data root: the files under data/ (ECU presets, ecukb/, tuningops/) are read next to the application; the root can be relocated with the MTR_DATA_DIR environment variable. data/ecukb/mtr_ecu.db (ECU/vehicle/DTC knowledge base) and data/tuningops/*.json (maintenance operations) are optional; when the file is missing, DTC Lookup and Maintenance mode silently disappear.
  • Local AI knowledge base (RAG): when data/ecukb/mtr_rag.db (SQLite FTS5) is present, the assistant appends the knowledge-base excerpts closest to your latest message to the prompt and offers the model a read-only kb_search tool. It is entirely local and uses no network. Without the database the assistant behaves exactly as before.
  • Offline map-name glossary: map-name translation first consults the built-in automotive acronym glossary (e.g. egr, lambda, ivvt, n_max); the Fast engine uses the glossary + Google chain, the Smart engine uses the selected AI model. Results are cached in the mapnames database.

docs.title: Checksum (export)
docs.text: With Project ▸ Correct checksums on export enabled, the checksum blocks detected when exporting a ROM are corrected automatically on the exported copy only (the project ROM is unchanged). The preference is stored under checksum/autoCorrectOnExport and persists between sessions; when it is off the correction asks before writing.

docs.title: AI providers
docs.text:
Field Meaning Provider Chosen from the list Key Provider-specific, stored locally (on Windows encrypted with DPAPI, bound to your user account) Base URL Optional, for OpenAI-compatible endpoints Model Chosen from the list, ⟳ refreshes it Effort Thinking budget sent to the model

Models are fetched live from the provider's /models endpoint. A warning is shown for free/trial models.

docs.title: Paths
docs.text:
Application data lives in the operating system's standard location:

Platform Location Windows %APPDATA%\MRC\MRC Tuner Studio Linux ~/.local/share/MRC Tuner Studio macOS ~/Library/Application Support/MRC Tuner Studio

That folder holds projects, autosaves, themes, the translation cache (mapnames.db) and the chat history. You can open it from the settings.

docs.title: Auto save
docs.text: With Auto Save enabled, edits are written after a configurable idle time. Temporary files go to autosave/, so data survives a crash.

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text:
• UI scale — interface scaling on high-DPI displays.
  • Defaults for byte order and data width.
  • Clear translation cache.
  • Debugging: builds with MTR_DEBUG_RPC=ON enable an in-app TCP channel and a file log; you can quote the relevant section in a bug report.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text: Settings live in the QSettings store under MRC / MRC Tuner Studio. If you have to edit them by hand, close the application first; the file is read on the next start.

docs.title: Maps show wrong values
docs.text:
Cause: wrong scaling or wrong base address.

  1. Open Map Properties and check factor and offset.
  2. If you imported from A2L, verify the base address — a wrong base opens every map in the wrong place.
  3. Compare a few cells of a map you know by heart.

docs.title: A map cannot be found
docs.text:
1. Try name patterns in Find ▸ Map (DKAT*, *LDR*).
  2. Scan the whole ROM with Miscellaneous ▸ Auto-detect Maps.
  3. Without an A2L, map boundaries simply are not recorded in a raw dump; if you know the address, define the map through Map Properties.
  4. Find ▸ Similar Files can locate the same map in a similar ROM so you can carry the address over.

docs.title: Checksum modules do not load
docs.text:
• On Windows, make sure ChecksumDLL sits next to mtr.exe.
  • Install the Microsoft Visual C++ 2005 SP1 (x86) runtime.
  • checksumhelper.exe may be missing; fetch it again.
  • On Linux/macOS there are no modules; only built-in MED17/EDC17 works.

docs.title: The ECU rejects the file
docs.text:
1. Check checksum validity.
  2. If CRCs are valid, the ECU's signature/integrity check may have engaged; that has to be verified with an external tool.
  3. Make sure this really is the right ROM variant (the same map name can live at a different address in another software version).
  4. If the A2L base address is wrong, the maps may have been written to the wrong place.

docs.title: The AI assistant refuses to write
docs.text:
• Check the permission mode: in Plan mode write tools are locked on purpose. Switch to Ask or Auto for write requests.
  • Narrow the request: "increase rows 3–7 of map X by 5%".
  • Is the provider/model reachable? Refresh the model list with ⟳ in Settings ▸ AI.

docs.title: Cannot connect to the AI (400 / 401 / 403 / 503)
docs.text: Code Meaning Fix 400 Request format Verify the model supports this endpoint 401 Key/validity Check the key and the base URL 403 Access restricted Your free-model quota may be exhausted 503 Service unavailable Try a different model or provider

docs.title: A file will not open
docs.text:
• Check the extension: projects must be .mtrp.
  • If the file is open elsewhere it may be locked — close the program and retry.
  • Windows Defender or your antivirus may have quarantined it.

docs.title: Translations come out incomplete
docs.text: The chain Google → Google (Chrome) → MyMemory is tried in order and the results are cached. Clear half-finished translations with Miscellaneous ▸ Clear Translation Cache and try again; you can correct results in the preview table.

docs.title: The interface feels slow
docs.text:
• With very large projects (tens of thousands of maps), narrow the Map Selection panel.
  • Closing the 2d waveform view reduces memory use.
  • Without a GPU driver the application falls back to a software rasteriser; a driver update makes a noticeable difference.

docs.title: Preparing a bug report
docs.text:
1. Describe the steps to reproduce.
  2. Give the ROM size and the map name (do not attach the ROM).
  3. State the version and operating system.
  4. Attach the relevant lines from mtr.log.
  5. Never share API keys.

docs.title: Formats read
docs.text: Format Extension Notes A2L / DAMOS .a2l .dam .damos ASAM MCD-2 MC; the most reliable path Intel HEX .hex Record addresses resolved, gaps preserved Motorola S-record .s19 .s28 .s37 S0–S9 records Raw ROM .bin .rom .ori .mpc Map boundaries are not recorded WinOLS .ols ROM + maps + axes + metadata KP pack .kp No ROM data; an open project is required TunerPro .xdf Definition file VAG .frf .sgo .odx .zip Encrypted content needs an AES key file CSV / JSON list .csv .json Map address lists Map pack .mtrpack MRC format Patch .mtrpatch MRC format Datalog .csv Channel list and time series

docs.title: Formats written
docs.text: Format Extension Notes Project .mtrp ROM + maps + history + metadata (container) Raw ROM .bin .rom Size and byte order preserved WinOLS .ols Import only — export is disabled in this build TunerPro .xdf Definition export Map pack .mtrpack / .csv Selected maps Map list .csv .json Name, address, dimensions Tuning report .html Old/new value comparison Theme .mtrtheme Palette definition

docs.title: The project container (.mtrp)
docs.text:
.mtrp is a binary container:

  • Header — magic (MTRP), format version, total size, TOC offset.
  • TOC — magic, offset and size of every block.
  • Blocks — ROM data, map definitions, metadata, history, styles.
  • Body checksum — to detect corruption.

Blocks are independent — each carries its own header and checksum. The current reader, however, verifies the whole-body checksum and therefore reads the entire file before decoding, so reading a single block still loads the whole file today.

docs.title: Patch format (.mtrpatch)
docs.text:
A JSON document:

{
  "format": "mtrpatch",
  "label": "Stage 1 — low RPM fuel maps",
  "maps": [
    {
      "name": "KRKTE_FIX",
      "address": "0x0012A340",
      "ref":  "0x0B0C0D0E",
      "new":  "0x0B0C1012"
    }
  ],
  "raw": []
}
  • ref — bytes before the change, used for verification.
  • new — bytes to write.
  • raw — raw byte patches outside maps (valid for the same software version).

docs.title: Map pack format (.mtrpack)
docs.text: Carries maps as name + address + scaling + values. The application matches them against the target ROM in three steps: explicit address, name, then the address stored in the pack.

docs.title: Scaling taken from A2L
docs.text: COMPU_METHOD uses COEFFS_LINEAR in the form f(x) = a·x + b. The application converts these coefficients directly into the map's factor and offset. Tabular conversions defined with COMPU_TAB_REF are supported too.

docs.title: Byte order
docs.text: Some A2L files declare BYTE_ORDER MSB_LAST, meaning the cell bytes are stored reversed. The application reads this as a property, but you can still change it manually with View ▸ Byte Order. A map read in the wrong order produces "meaningless" values that are surprisingly easy to miss.

docs.title: Appendix — Glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning A2L ASAM MCD-2 MC definition file; pins down address, size and scaling. Axis The physical meaning of a map's rows/columns. Byte order The order in which the bytes of a cell are stored. Checksum Integrity value inside the ROM; recalculated after changes. COMPU_METHOD A2L rule for converting to a physical value. Container The project format keeping ROM, maps, history and metadata in one file (.mtrp). Curve One-dimensional map; type CURVE. Differences Panel listing the differences between two versions/ROMs. Linked ROM A reference ROM attached to the project for comparison. Limp mode The ECU's protective state after a failed integrity check. Map A table of adjacent bytes in the ROM. MTRP Magic value / format name of the project container. Offset The additive part of a scaling rule. Patch File carrying specific byte/map changes (.mtrpatch). Physical domain Values after scaling has been applied — what you see. Scaling Factor and offset that convert a raw byte to a physical value. Slider limits The range outside which cell values may not move. Snapshot The complete project state at one moment; a return point. SOI Start Of Image — the beginning of a data block in A2L. TOC Block directory inside the project container. Value map Single-cell (1×1) scaling or setting value. Cursor sync Keeps two compared views on the same row.

docs.title: Abbreviations
docs.text: Short Meaning ECU Electronic Control Unit ROM Read Only Memory — the flash holding the ECU software DTC Diagnostic Trouble Code RAM The ECU's working memory STD_AXIS Standard, evenly spaced axis definition COM_AXIS Common-reference (irregular) axis definition MSB_FIRST Most significant byte first (big endian) MSB_LAST Least significant byte first (little endian)

docs.title: Common map-name patterns
docs.text:
Pattern Usually indicates DKAT* / KAT* Catalyst monitoring thresholds LDRXN*, LDR* Load / boost request maps N_LIMIT* Rev limiter VMAX* Speed limiter AGR* EGR flow / valve position maps DPF* Diesel particulate filter pressure / soot KRKTE* Fuel correction (lambda/cycle) maps

Tip

Do not trust these patterns blindly: always open the search results and check the map's dimensions and axes first. The same name can mean something different in another ROM.
